stem:
Sameer has trapezium $PQRS$ with $PQ\parallel SR$ and $\angle P=75^{\circ}$. Angle $S$ lies on the same non-parallel side $PS$.

Which claim correctly gives $\angle S$?

options.text: Report the words parallel sides as the measure of $\angle S$.
$\angle S$ equals $105^{\circ}$, because the angles on the same non-parallel side between the parallel sides add to $180^{\circ}$.
The parallel sides $PQ\parallel SR$ are produced by the $105^{\circ}$ angle.

teacher.key_rationale: Between parallel sides, co-interior angles on leg PS are supplementary: 75°+∠S=180°, so ∠S=105°. Copying 75°, naming parallel sides as a measure, or reversing cause each miss that pair.
